title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (September 2026 data) — the only edition of this index that lands inside Thanksgiving week
source: EST: the publisher's own stated schedule rule, re-read direct from a primary today. press.spglobal.com's June-2026-data release (2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 90,693 bytes), states it verbatim: `The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET.` November 2026's Tuesdays are the 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24th, so the last is 2026-11-24, and the release's own two-month reporting lag puts September 2026 data on it. Corroborated on REALIZED dates from prnewswire.com's Case-Shiller listing and per-item `datePublished` stamps, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (search HTTP 200, 220,741 bytes; twelve item pages HTTP 200, 262,592-271,781 bytes each): twelve consecutive realized editions 2025-09-30 through 2026-08-25, every one a last Tuesday — including 2025-11-25, the last Tuesday of November 2025 and the direct precedent for this date. Filed `estimate` on the taxonomy gap (CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs has no member for a private index provider) and on this lane's no-self-confirm limit; the date is the publisher's own rule and is not in doubt. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, after reading the single proposal that carried it (proposals/case-shiller-hpi-2026-11-24.from-case-shiller-hpi-2026-12-29.json), which is now shadowed. WHAT IS UNIQUE TO THIS EDITION, and it is arithmetic: the last Tuesday of November is ALWAYS either Thanksgiving minus 2 days or Thanksgiving plus 5 — never anything else, computed for every year 1990-2050 (26 pre, 35 post). 2026 is a `pre` year, so this edition publishes on the Tuesday of Thanksgiving week: the market closes Thursday 2026-11-26 and half-days Friday 2026-11-27. Unlike the December edition, it can never collide with a market holiday at all — Thanksgiving is a Thursday and November carries no fixed-date market closure — so this print's release-day sample is NOT survivorship-filtered, which is the exact complement of what case-shiller-hpi-2026-12-29 measured for its own date. THE ONE MEASURED EFFECT ON THE SESSION IS A HOLIDAY ARTIFACT, NOT THIS PRINT: on CBOE's own history the Tuesday before Thanksgiving carries VIX9D/VIX at a 0.8592 median against a 0.9416 all-session median (n=15, 2011-2025, p=0.0053 by 20,000-iteration randomization), 13 of 15 below 1.00 — a deeper front-curve compression than the Christmas-week result the fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 lane measured (0.906 vs 0.942). It is disambiguated rather than assumed: the effect is present in both the release-day subset (0.8503, n=7) and the non-release-day subset (0.8765, n=8), and the two halves of this series' own November editions differ by it directly (pre-Thanksgiving 0.8503 vs post-Thanksgiving 0.9860, p=0.0036). Every other tape class is null. ATTRIBUTION IS THE WORST OF THE THREE TRACKED CASE-SHILLER EDITIONS: the day itself carries fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24 (the only `confirmed` entry in the corridor), consumer-confidence-2026-11-24 at 10:00, a 5Y note and a 2Y FRN — and the NEXT morning, 2026-11-25, is the compressed Wednesday Thanksgiving creates, carrying gdp-q3-2026-second and pce (both `high`) plus durable goods, new-home sales, the Beige Book and a 7Y note. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, `low` impact, the date is `estimate`.
